text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the family history of joint swelling, I suspect hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and IX levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, this rules out hemophilia A and B, suggesting a different coagulation issue. Do you have a history of prolonged bleeding after other minor injuries or surgeries?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal factor levels and family history of joint swelling point towards a platelet function defect, possibly Von Willebrand Disease. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand factor antigen and activity levels

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor VIII, IX, and Von Willebrand factor levels, I suspect a platelet function disorder like Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Platelet function analysis and platelet count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet function analysis: Abnormal aggregation to ADP, epinephrine, and collagen; normal aggregation to ristocetin. Platelet count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count with abnormal aggregation to ADP, epinephrine, and collagen but normal ristocetin response is classic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia. Do you experience excessive bleeding after dental procedures or minor cuts in your daily life?
